evidence: OrderModule.ts: createOrderUseCases builds PlaceOrderUseCase, GetOrderUseCase, ListOrdersUseCase and ChangeOrderStatusUseCase and returns them as OrderUseCases.
lookups.ts: requireOrder and requireProducts are used by GetOrderUseCase, ChangeOrderStatusUseCase and PlaceOrderUseCase; none of them repeat the NotFoundError checks inline.
OrderMapper.ts: toOrderDto is the only place Order becomes OrderDto, and all four use cases call it.
ChangeOrderStatusUseCase.ts: the TARGET_STATUS table is defined only here, and stock handling is delegated to stockEffectOf and StockAllocator.
orderCommandParsers.ts: parsePlaceOrderCommand returns the PlaceOrderCommand and OrderItemInput types from OrderDtos.ts.
ListOrdersUseCase.ts: checks the status with the domain's isOrderStatus and ORDER_STATUSES rather than its own list.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All files in src/application/orders handle one concern: order use cases. The four use case classes each sit behind an interface and are wired together in one place, OrderModule.ts (createOrderUseCases). The use cases always go through the module's shared helpers: lookups.ts for loading entities and throwing not-found errors, and OrderMapper.ts (toOrderDto) for building DTOs. None of them repeat repository-miss handling or DTO mapping inline. The request and response shapes live together in OrderDtos.ts. The action-to-status table (TARGET_STATUS) appears only in ChangeOrderStatusUseCase. Stock rules are delegated to domain code (stockEffectOf and StockAllocator) rather than restated here. orderCommandParsers.ts only builds the PlaceOrderCommand defined in OrderDtos. Two minor points don't amount to duplicating an invariant: productIn and requireProducts both throw NotFoundError('Product'), but over different sources (a loaded map versus the repository), and ListOrdersUseCase validates the status inline using the domain's isOrderStatus and ORDER_STATUSES.
